Question Choices: Find the center of (x + 4)^2/25 + (y - 1)^2/4 = 1. Enter x then y.
Hints: Read h from x - h and k from y - k.|The signs flip.
Solution: For an axis-aligned ellipse, read the center from x-h and y-k. Positive denominators are squared semi-axis lengths; the larger one gives the major-axis direction. Add and subtract each semi-axis length along its own coordinate axis to locate vertices and co-vertices. x+4=x-(-4), so h=-4; y-1 gives k=1.

Question Choices: For the circle (x - 1)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 49, what is the center? Enter x then y.
Hints: Read h and k from the squares.|The signs flip.
Solution: Match (x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2. The center is (h,k); the radius is the positive square root of the right-hand side. x-1 gives h=1 and y+3=y-(-3) gives k=-3.
